newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's changes lead U.S. advertising agency.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's changes lead U.S. advertising agency.

text.p: Fast-food giant McDonald's Corp., in the midst of a realignment of its domestic business, Tuesday changed its lead advertising agency in the United States for the first time in 15 years.

McDonald's, which has an estimated U.S. advertising budget of $600 million, said it chose DDB Needham, a unit of Omnicom Group Inc., as its lead advertising agency in the United States, responsible for all adult and promotion advertising activity.
DDB Needham takes over as lead agency from Leo Burnett Co., effective immediately.
"We will be looking for an overall theme and brand positioning coming from DDB Needham," Brad Ball, senior vice president for McDonald's USA marketing, said in an interview.
Burnett had been the lead advertising agency for McDonald's since the fall of 1981. DDB Needham previously had the lead from 1970 to 1981.

Leo Burnett will continue to work on the McDonald's U.S. advertising account, developing marketing strategies for its children's, "tween," and Ronald McDonald business. The "tween" market includes pre-teens and young teenagers.
McDonald's has a total U.S. advertising budget of about $600 million, which includes national, regional and speciality promotions targeted at Hispanic and black consumers.
Ball said no changes have been made in McDonald's regional and speciality advertising nor in its international advertising.

"Looking at McDonald's domestic business, this represents another element of the changing of the guard, starting with senior leadership," Merrill Lynch analyst Peter Oakes said of the change in lead advertising agencies.

Earlier this month, McDonald's announced plans to reorganize its U.S. business into five geographic divisions with more autonomy. In addition, Jack Greenberg, chairman of the McDonald's USA unit, took on the additional title of chief executive officer, replacing company veteran Ed Rensi. The company said Rensi is retiring as president and chief executive of McDonald's USA.

The change in lead advertising agencies also comes less than three months after McDonald's pulled most of its "Campaign 55," which had been expected to be a long-term price promotion in the United States.

McDonald's cancelled the lunch and dinner portions of Campaign 55 -- which offered featured hamburgers for 55 cents when a customer also bought a drink and french fries -- after six weeks when it failed to build customer traffic.
McDonald's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $53.875 in late consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Omnicon fell 44 cents to $65.69, also on the NYSE.

Analysts said DDB Needham, as the lead advertising agency, must help McDonald's draft marketing and promotions that build on the fast-food chain's strengths such as convenience, consistency and service.
But the challenge remains for McDonald's to improve its food products as competition in the U.S. fast-food market intensifies, said Natwest Markets analyst Damon Brundage.
"We know the problem is the product," Brundage added.
McDonald's executives have said the company is looking at ways to improve its production system to make fresher, tastier food.
